en: Kāmāvacaradukādi (The Couplets on Sense-Sphere Phenomena, etc.)
Dependent on a state belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*), a state not belonging to the sense sphere arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*) … three.
Dependent on a state not belonging to the sense sphere, a state not belonging to the non-sense-sphere arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are nine;

under object condition, four; under predominance condition, five … pe … under mutuality condition, six … pe … under prenascence and repetition conditions, two … pe … under non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a fine-material-sphere state, a non-fine-material-sphere state arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a non-fine-material-sphere state, a non-non-fine-material-sphere state arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root: nine; under object: four; under predominance: five... mutual: six... prenascence and repetition: two... non-disappearance: nine.
Dependent on a state belonging to the formless sphere (*arūpāvacara*), a state not belonging to the formless sphere arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*)—three [cases].
Dependent on a state not belonging to the formless sphere, a state not belonging to the formless sphere arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state belonging both to the formless sphere and not to the formless sphere, a state not belonging to the formless sphere arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the ripening condition, two ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.
